passage:
Mohit threw his spoon and screamed. "No! No!"
"Mohit, stop that," Ayesha said. "Eat your khichdi nicely."
He shoved the bowl away and grabbed at her plate.
"Hey! That's rude."
Dadi looked up from the stove. "Ayesha, when did he last eat?"
Ayesha glanced at the clock. "Breakfast. The market took forever."
"He's hungry, not naughty."
Ayesha cooled a spoonful and held it out. Mohit gulped it, then another. His sobs slowed to hiccups.

qa.q: Why had Mohit gone so long without eating?
What was Mohit feeling when he grabbed at Ayesha's plate?
qa.a: He was hungry and distressed, and grabbing and screaming were the only ways he could show it.

qa.q: What worked better than scolding, and why?
qa.a: Feeding him a cooled spoonful right away; a hungry toddler calms once food arrives, not after a telling-off.

qa.q: How does Ayesha read the screaming at first?
qa.a: She reads it as rudeness and scolds him, until Dadi's question makes her see he is hungry.

grounding: Shows a hungry toddler who cannot say so screaming, throwing and grabbing, and food ending the outburst faster than discipline.

passage: Creche note for Pema's family, Friday. Pema arrived late and missed our morning snack. By late morning she was snatching other children's biscuits, throwing her cup and refusing even the banana she loves. She couldn't tell us why. The book showed nothing since an early breakfast. I sat her down with fruit and rice; she ate in silence and was soon building towers again. On late days we will feed her as soon as she arrives. Vijay (creche teacher)

qa.q: What did Pema refuse even though she usually loves it?
What was Pema feeling when she threw her cup?
qa.a: She was hungry and upset but could not say so, so the distress came out as snatching and throwing.

qa.q: What plan did Vijay make, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: To give Pema something to eat as soon as she arrives on late days; keeping food regular can stop the tantrum before it starts.

qa.q: How might the other children have been affected?
qa.a: They had biscuits snatched from them and may have felt upset or confused, not knowing Pema was just hungry.

grounding: Illustrates a hungry toddler showing need through grabbing, throwing and refusing food, and regular feeding settling her.
